questions: Why does the same angle fraction give both the arc and the sector area?
What fraction of the circle is a 90 degree sector?
segments.say: Arc length and sector area. A sector is a fraction of the whole circle, and the angle tells you the fraction. Keep your student notes open at the arc length and sector definitions for this scene.

questions: Why is the factor one third and not one half?
Which height counts: the slant edge or the vertical height?
segments.say: Pyramid volume, revealed. Three pyramids fill the prism on the same base, so the volume is one third of base area times height. Now try the pyramid question on the worksheet in pairs.

questions: Why is the radius cubed in the sphere formula?
What happens to the volume if the radius doubles?
segments.say: Sphere volume. Slices of the sphere stack into 4/3 pi r cubed. Check the sphere definition in your student notes and say the formula back to your partner.

questions: How many radius-3 disks fit inside a radius-6 disk?
What is the correct multiplier on area when any radius doubles?
segments.say: A common mistake: doubling r doubles area. Lay the small disk over the big one and count how many fit. Then take the exit ticket on your own - its first question revisits exactly this claim.
segments.watchFor: Doubling the radius doubles the area of a circle. Listen for it in pair talk and watch for it on the exit ticket: Doubling a length doubles lengths, so area feels like it doubles too. Send them back to the two disks and the correct turn: Area scales with the square of the radius: double the radius and the area quadruples.
